sections.context: The comprehensive product plan defines a clean Rust, Tauri, and Leptos platform spanning exact catalog history, KiCad libraries, project intelligence, PocketBase collaboration, inventory, procurement, and design reuse. Existing CSV and CAD data are import inputs rather than an executable Python or PyQt compatibility contract. A flat task dump or layer-by-layer rewrite would obscure user outcomes, create false dependencies, and prevent agents from completing independently testable vertical slices in the isolated Linux environment.
sections.approach: Organize delivery as ten outcome-oriented epics. Decompose each epic into tracer bullets that cross domain, persistence, application, UI, and integration seams far enough to prove a real workflow. Rust, Tauri, and Leptos are the only supported application implementation, PocketBase is the selected team backend, and Linux is the primary complete AFK integration lane. Mainline tools and KiCad 10 are pinned while scheduled compatibility lanes detect upgrades. Every frontend seed owns its automated journeys, semantic and accessibility assertions, deterministic screenshots, and agent visual self-review. Windows and macOS are later native release gates rather than blockers for every Linux tracer. Attach dependencies only between concrete child seeds where execution truly requires earlier evidence or an interface.

alternatives.name: Mirror every product-plan bullet as a seed
alternatives.rejected_because: It would create a noisy backlog of layer tasks without independently verifiable outcomes or useful ready-queue ordering.

alternatives.name: Chain roadmap phases as a strict waterfall
alternatives.rejected_because: Many domain experiments and adapters can proceed safely in parallel; blocking whole epics would hide valid work and slow feedback.

alternatives.name: Keep the prototype operational until parity
alternatives.rejected_because: Python and PyQt are not supported product scope. Immutable input fixtures and loss-detecting imports preserve valuable data without turning prototype behavior into a migration gate.

alternatives.name: Track work in Markdown checklists
alternatives.rejected_because: Seeds is the git-native source of truth for status, acceptance, dependencies, and readiness; parallel checklists would drift.

steps.title: Prove a Linux-first Rust product foundation
Give Engineers an exact revisioned KiCad catalog
Protect known-good baselines and close engineering defects
Adopt release switch and roll back libraries safely
Turn saved KiCad projects into actionable parts intelligence
Let small teams collaborate safely from desktop and web
Know usable inventory without false precision
Turn material demand into reviewed supplier handoffs
Reuse proven circuit blocks across organizations
Validate and release the Rust product across Linux, Windows, and macOS

risks: A clean implementation can silently lose uncommon source data; every import tracer uses immutable fixtures, field and byte manifests, and actionable parity reports.
Premature dependencies can make independent discovery and domain work disappear from the ready queue.
PocketBase or supplier assumptions can age quickly; versions are pinned, upgrades are rehearsed, and unresolved behavior remains a focused investigation seed rather than an untested fact.
Linux integration success can conceal native path, dialog, credential, installer, filesystem, or graphics failures; Windows and macOS remain explicit distribution gates.

Screenshot self-review can become ceremonial; seed acceptance requires a stable state matrix, semantic and accessibility assertions, retained diffs, recorded critique, and iteration on every material issue.
acceptance: Every confirmed product capability and roadmap exit condition is owned by exactly one outcome epic or an explicitly referenced cross-epic acceptance check.

Each epic is decomposed into independently verifiable vertical tracer seeds before implementation begins, and dependencies are attached at the narrowest concrete seed level so the ready queue exposes useful work.
Rust, Tauri, and Leptos are the only supported application implementation; existing catalog and CAD inputs remain read-only fixtures, and no Python or PyQt compatibility gate is required.

PocketBase is the only planned team-backend adapter and its protected commands, authorization, realtime recovery, migrations, upgrades, S3-compatible backup, and blank-environment restore receive real-process evidence.
Every frontend seed declares and runs its browser or native journey, semantic and accessibility assertions, materially distinct screenshots, and an agent visual self-review with required iteration.
The Linux AFK lane is isolated from host KiCad and user state, pins exact tool and KiCad versions, emits a complete evidence manifest, and has a separate scheduled newest-KiCad-10 compatibility lane.

Before Windows or macOS distribution, that native platform passes its release matrix for builds, paths, dialogs, credentials, installers, updater, filesystems, process launch, and host KiCad discovery.
No implementation seed authorizes unsafe mutation of an open KiCad project, editable library, immutable release, or operating-system-installed library.

sections.context: The supported product now begins directly with Rust, Tauri, and Leptos. The existing CSV catalog and local CAD assets remain valuable migration inputs, but Python and PyQt are not supported runtimes or parity targets. PocketBase is the selected team backend. Before catalog implementation expands, the project needs reproducible evidence that real source data, the Rust desktop, KiCad 10, PocketBase collaboration, and S3-compatible recovery all work in an isolated Linux environment suitable for unattended agent execution.
sections.approach: Capture the checked-in catalog and CAD assets as loss-detecting Rust import fixtures without executing or preserving the PyQt application. In parallel, build one pinned Linux AFK stack containing the Rust and Tauri toolchain, KiCad 10 and its official libraries, PocketBase, MinIO, X11 virtual-display support, and the native UI driver. Use that environment for two vertical tracers: a real-catalog Tauri and Leptos UI journey with screenshots and agent visual review, and a PocketBase collaboration and S3-compatible backup and restore journey. The official KiCad container is authoritative for CLI integration; a clean Ubuntu/X11 runner owns real GUI smoke coverage. Linux is the primary integration environment, while Windows and macOS remain later native release gates.

alternatives.name: Keep PyQt running as the migration oracle
alternatives.rejected_because: Python and PyQt are no longer supported scope; checked-in source data and expected artifacts provide a smaller and more durable import contract.

alternatives.name: Continue comparing backend providers
alternatives.rejected_because: PocketBase has been selected for its maturity and documentation, so remaining work should test its real operational behavior rather than maintain a hypothetical provider swap.

alternatives.name: Use the developer's installed KiCad and floating latest dependencies
alternatives.rejected_because: Host state prevents parallel unattended execution, while floating versions make failures irreproducible. Mainline runs use exact pins and a separate compatibility check reports newer KiCad 10 releases.

alternatives.name: Mock PocketBase, S3, and KiCad in every integration test
alternatives.rejected_because: Unit tests may fake application-owned interfaces, but recovery, migrations, file compatibility, and GUI launch require the real external implementations in the isolated stack.

steps.title: Capture loss-detecting Rust import fixtures
Boot an isolated Linux AFK product stack
Exercise the real catalog and exact CAD previews through the Rust desktop
Prove PocketBase collaboration and S3-compatible recovery

risks: A fixture can accidentally encode Python implementation details; assertions must cover stable source fields, bytes, semantic content, diagnostics, and generated KiCad artifacts.

A floating latest KiCad package can invalidate reproducibility; every run records exact package versions and image digests, while a scheduled compatibility lane tests the newest available KiCad 10 release.

Containerized GUI tests can hide native desktop problems; the official container is authoritative only for CLI integration, Linux desktop infrastructure provides real GUI smoke evidence, and Windows and macOS remain explicit release gates.

Screenshot comparison alone can miss behavior and accessibility failures; UI journeys combine semantic assertions, accessibility checks, stable screenshots, and an agent-written visual critique followed by iteration.

A database-only backup can appear successful while losing managed files; recovery tests verify relational records, PocketBase-managed files, separately stored objects where enabled, and hashes after restoring into blank isolated state.
acceptance: Rust tests inventory all 21 current categories and 178 rows, substitutes, local CAD references and assets, byte and semantic hashes, and the intentional distinction between 21 generated SQLite tables and 19 descriptor entries; a controlled fixture mutation produces an actionable field-level diff without invoking Python or PyQt.

One documented command starts a clean, parallel-safe stack with exact versions of Rust, Node, Tauri system dependencies, KiCad 10 and official libraries, PocketBase, and MinIO; the run emits a machine-readable version and image-digest manifest.

The AFK stack mounts no host KiCad configuration, library installation, Windows home directory, production credentials, or PocketBase state; isolated volumes and sentinel checks prove the host remains untouched, and teardown removes test state unless preservation on failure is requested.

The official KiCad container runs kicad-cli against representative fixtures, while an ephemeral Ubuntu/X11 lane launches the KiCad 10 GUI and captures logs and a diagnostic screenshot without relying on the Windows host installation.
The Tauri and Leptos application searches at least 20,000 rows within the product target and previews the exact selected symbol and footprint through an automated native Linux journey.

Every frontend journey emits test results, accessibility evidence, and screenshots of all materially distinct states at stable viewports; the implementing agent records a visual and UX self-review and iterates until no material issue remains.

The real PocketBase service executes authentication, an optimistic protected command, second-client realtime notification, stale conflict, disconnect and checkpoint reconciliation, and a migration or upgrade rehearsal.

PocketBase backup artifacts are written to an isolated MinIO S3-compatible bucket; after deleting disposable PocketBase state, restore into a blank instance reproduces records, managed files, separately protected objects where enabled, and expected hashes.
No alternate-backend adapter, comparison harness, Python runtime, or PyQt compatibility gate is introduced.

sections.context: The checked-in CSV catalog and local CAD libraries are source inputs for the new Rust product, not an active Python or PyQt workflow that must remain compatible. The target platform needs stable part and asset identities, immutable revision history, optimistic conflict handling, exact provenance and licensing, and a deterministic KiCad projection. The safest path is to prove the model on one representative real category inside the isolated Linux, PocketBase, and KiCad environment before attempting a complete import.
sections.approach: Start with the existing resistor category and its local CAD references. Import it idempotently into canonical Catalog records with stable IDs, full initial snapshots, asset/blob/revision separation, and an explicit Change Set, while producing a zero-loss report against the source-fixture oracle. Then exercise one real Engineer edit through the Tauri and Leptos UI, protected command boundary, audit, conflict, restore, PocketBase realtime plus checkpoint reconciliation, and staged KiCad projection. Prove schema-bearing taxonomy and reviewed supplier-category mapping on the same slice. Only after those contracts pass, import the complete catalog and demonstrate deterministic projection. Source CSVs and local libraries remain byte-for-byte unchanged throughout the pilot.

alternatives.name: Design and migrate the full schema in one pass
alternatives.rejected_because: It would combine identity, revisions, assets, taxonomy, backend, UI, and projection risks before any real end-to-end path proves their contracts.

alternatives.name: Keep CSV rows as the canonical mutable model
alternatives.rejected_because: CSV cannot safely express optimistic commands, immutable history, exact asset bindings, team authorization, or auditable restores.

alternatives.name: Use event deltas as the only historical representation
alternatives.rejected_because: Immutable full revision snapshots make exact reconstruction, diff, restore, migration, and KiCad projection simpler and more robust for this domain.

steps.title: Import one complete legacy category into canonical revisions
Publish conflict and restore one Managed Part with exact CAD revisions
Classify one part through versioned taxonomy and reviewed supplier mapping
Prove lossless full-catalog migration and deterministic KiCad projection

risks: A normalization pass can silently discard blank strings, uncommon columns, category-specific fields, substitutes, or intentionally unprojected categories; every import produces a field-level loss report.
Logical assets, stored bytes, and semantic revisions can be conflated; raw blob hashes, revision snapshot hashes, provenance, and license declarations have distinct authority and tests.
Operational supplier, inventory, scan, or draft facts can accidentally create catalog revisions; revision commands accept only semantic catalog changes.
A projection failure can corrupt active KiCad state; generation always stages, validates, and atomically activates an isolated test-owned target with rollback evidence.
A visually plausible catalog can still be unusable or inaccessible; every new Tauri or Leptos state requires semantic, keyboard, accessibility, and inspected screenshot evidence.
acceptance: The current resistor category imports idempotently with stable part IDs, immutable IPNs, initial full Part Revisions, exact local CAD asset bindings, source-row provenance, explicit license disposition, and one reasoned Change Set; unresolved references are diagnostics rather than lost data.

An Engineer publishes a semantic edit with expected revision and correlation ID; the transaction creates one Change Set, successor Part and any needed Asset Revisions, a head update, and an Audit Event, while no-op, duplicate, unauthorized, and stale commands behave deterministically.
The desktop shows semantic diff, conflict, and history and restores by creating a new successor revision; a second client converges through PocketBase realtime plus checkpoint reconciliation.

A schema-bearing Catalog Category validates the representative part without changing its stable IPN Family, and an externally observed DigiKey, Mouser, or LCSC category becomes a reviewed mapping rather than an automatic silent reclassification.

The complete source catalog, substitutes, assets, origins, and license declarations import with a zero-loss oracle report and regenerate semantically equivalent staged SQLite and database-library artifacts deterministically.

The checked-in CSV catalog and local libraries remain byte-for-byte unchanged during the isolated canonical pilot; generated projections exist only in test-owned paths, and no Python or PyQt runtime dependency is introduced.

Every Tauri or Leptos state introduced by this epic has an automated native Linux journey, semantic and accessibility assertions, screenshots for materially distinct states, and a recorded agent visual self-review followed by any required iteration.

sections.context: Teams own material distributed across local labs, assembly houses, partner-managed accounts, and stock in transit. Existing planning distinguishes physical carriers and estimated quantities, but it does not yet separate ownership, custody, source, site, restrictions, reservations, or a standing local prototype floor. Without those distinctions, a global available total can over-promise restricted stock, transfers can double-count, aggregate partner balances can gain fictional traceability, and permanent fake reservations make local coverage impossible to reason about. The product plan and Inventory glossary define the required language and low-click progressive-disclosure UX.
sections.approach: Deliver four vertical tracer bullets through the real Rust domain, PocketBase contract boundary, Leptos/Rust-UI surface, and AFK Linux evidence path. Establish a physical Stock Holding and confidence ledger first; then add a partner aggregate position and distributed overview; then prove Material Reservations and project-derived Stock Floors; finally prove restricted-pool transfer and reconciliation. Every slice uses independent Recorded Owner, Custodian, Inventory Site, supplier/source, Stock State, and Use Constraints. Reservations and floors affect demand-specific allocation but never Stock Movements. Common workflows remain compact, while site, carrier, evidence, and history detail appear progressively in a side sheet.

alternatives.name: One global quantity per part
alternatives.rejected_because: It cannot preserve custody, location, confidence, traceability, partner-pool restrictions, or local prototype coverage and would produce unsafe availability answers.

alternatives.name: Treat every external balance as a Stock Container
alternatives.rejected_because: It invents reels, lots, and date codes that the partner did not report and makes reconciliation misleading.

alternatives.name: Represent reservations and local buffers as Stock Movements
alternatives.rejected_because: Neither changes physical quantity or custody; mixing them into the ledger corrupts on-hand arithmetic and obscures their different lifecycles.

alternatives.name: Build schema layers before any user journey
alternatives.rejected_because: Layer-only work delays validation of terminology, policy, integration seams, accessibility, and the low-click UI until the model is expensive to change.

steps.title: Receive and estimate one physical reel end to end
See one part across local and partner-held stock
Protect local prototype coverage while reserving one build
Transfer and reconcile one restricted partner stock pool

risks: Seller/source, Recorded Owner, Custodian, and Inventory Site could collapse into one overloaded vendor or location field.
Expected quantities or stale partner balances could be shown as exact or universally allocatable.
Reservations, Stock Floors, quarantine, or workflow locations could leak back into the physical Stock Movement ledger as dispositions.
Dispatch, destination receipt, and Procurement inbound supply could count the same pieces more than once.
A broad inventory screen could become a scroll-heavy ERP form and violate the product's few-click interaction goal.
Partner adapters could fabricate carrier-level traceability or silently overwrite earlier source evidence.
AFK screenshot comparison could pass while semantics, focus, or demand-specific labels remain wrong.
acceptance: A user can receive, label, observe, and reconcile one physical reel while the immutable ledger preserves quantity confidence and provenance.

One Managed Part can be shown across a local physical holding and a partner aggregate balance with independent Recorded Owner, Custodian, Inventory Site, source, restrictions, freshness, and confidence; no fictional carrier or lot is created.
The overview and part side sheet separate local, partner-held, reserved, protected, quarantined, and in-transit facts and calculate Allocatable Quantity only for a named demand policy.

A user can set a direct local Stock Floor or preview one derived from N builds of an exact Project Revision, then reserve a production build without changing on-hand quantity or silently consuming the floor.
A restricted partner pool cannot satisfy incompatible demand or mix with a prohibited pool; dispatch and receipt move stock through one in-transit position and conserve quantity under retry.

Each child Seed has domain/property tests, real pinned PocketBase adapter coverage where applicable, WebdriverIO browser/native journeys, accessibility assertions, deterministic screenshots and diffs, an agent visual-review note, and a cargo xtask AFK command with retained evidence.
The common Receive, Move, Reserve, and Keep local workflows fit the 1280x800 acceptance viewport with bounded scrolling, keyboard operation, visible exceptions, and no unbounded master form.
Documentation, Inventory glossary, Seed dependency graph, Mulch guidance, and implemented behavior use the same canonical terms and pass their validation commands.
